title: A terminal cylinder with selected vertical markings is marked anodyne
statement: Use small simplicial sets, and standard simplices as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and marked simplicial sets and marked-anodyne maps as in [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus], in the fixed universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A simplex is nondegenerate if it is not the image of a degeneracy map from a lower degree. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, let $K'\subseteq K$ be a simplicial subset, and let $A\subseteq K_0$ be a set of vertices. Let $E$ consist of all degenerate edges of $K\times\Delta^1$ together with the vertical edges $\{a\}\times\Delta^1$ for $a\in A$. Put $B=(K'\times\Delta^1)\cup(K\times\{1\})$, with the union formed inside $K\times\Delta^1$. Suppose that every nondegenerate simplex of $K$ either belongs to $K'$ or has its final vertex in $A$; the final vertex of an $r$-simplex is its restriction along $\{r\}\hookrightarrow[r]$. Then the inclusion $(B,E\cap B_1)\hookrightarrow(K\times\Delta^1,E)$ is marked anodyne.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1.9 (with its simplex input Lemma 3.2.1.8), printed p. 173. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag states this marked simplicial result.

proof.text: We will use marked pushouts and increasing unions in their explicit form. Form the underlying simplicial pushout degree by degree and mark exactly the images of the marked edges of its inputs. A map out is simplicial and preserves marked edges exactly when its two restrictions do; this proves the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For increasing unions use the degreewise union and the union of the markings, with the same restriction test. Simplicial operators on these constructions are induced by those on the inputs, as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. These rules apply to marked simplicial sets as defined in [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus]; in particular a pushout does not automatically mark every edge whose image later becomes degenerate under some other map.

source.place: Definition 3.1.0.1, marked simplicial sets; elementary marked-colimit details for the simplex-by-simplex argument of Lemma 3.2.1.9

proof.text: First fix $n\geq0$ and prove the simplex cylinder calculation needed below. On $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$ mark only the degenerate edges and $e_n=\{n\}\times\Delta^1$; denote this marking by $E_n$. Put $D_n=(\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^1)\cup(\Delta^n\times\{1\})$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-prism-boundary] with $m=n$ and exchange the two product coordinates. It gives $D_n=X_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq X_{n+1}=\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$, attaching $\Lambda_{q+1}^{n+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{n+1}$ at step $q$. The attaching simplex $\tau_q$ has vertices $(j,0)$ for $j\leq q$ and $(j-1,1)$ for $j>q$. Give every $X_q$ the marking induced by $E_n$. These are the actual pushout maps supplied by the cited statement, not just a decomposition of the vertex sets.

source.place: Kerodon Lemma 3.1.2.12, assertions (a), (b) and the displayed sigma maps; coordinate exchange supplies the prism used in HTT Lemma 3.2.1.8

proof.text: For $q<n$ the horn index satisfies $0<q+1<n+1$, so the minimally marked horn inclusion is generator (i) of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus]. The only repeated first coordinate among distinct vertices of $\tau_q$ occurs at positions $q,q+1$, with first coordinate $q$, so its only vertical edge is over $q$, not over $n$. Consequently $\tau_q$ carries no nondegenerate edge into $e_n$. Since here $n\geq1$, the edge $e_n$ already belongs to $\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\subseteq X_0$ with its marking. Thus the underlying pushout from Step 2, when made a pushout of the minimally marked inner horn, has exactly the induced $E_n$ marking on $X_{q+1}$: it keeps the old marked edge and adds no new nondegenerate marked edge. By Step 1 this is a marked pushout and hence is marked anodyne.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1.8, simplex input; explicit inner-horn part of its marked prism calculation using Definition 3.1.1.1(i)

proof.text: For $q=n$ the horn is $\Lambda_{n+1}^{n+1}$. The only vertical edge of $\tau_n$ joins its final two vertices $(n,0),(n,1)$ and is exactly $e_n$. Use generator (ii) of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus], with its final edge marked. Its horn restriction preserves markings into $X_n$, and the pushout marking on $X_{n+1}$ is precisely $E_n$, by Step 1. When $n\geq1$ the final edge is in the horn (it lies in the face omitting vertex $0$), and is already marked in $X_0$; when $n=0$ the horn is $\Lambda_1^1=\{1\}$ and this pushout adds the single marked interval. Thus this last attachment is marked anodyne as well. Closure under finite compositions proves $(D_n,E_n\cap(D_n)_1)\hookrightarrow(\Delta^n\times\Delta^1,E_n)$ is marked anodyne for every $n\geq0$.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1.8, simplex input; explicit final-horn calculation using Definition 3.1.1.1(ii), including dimension zero

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to $K'\hookrightarrow K$. It supplies $Z_0=K'\subseteq Z_1\subseteq\cdots$ with union $K$, and the map $Z_n\hookrightarrow Z_{n+1}$ is the pushout of the boundary inclusions for the missing nondegenerate $n$-simplices $\sigma:\Delta^n\to K$. Each such $\sigma$ has final vertex $\sigma(n)\in A$ by the hypothesis of the item. Inside $K\times\Delta^1$ put $T_n=(Z_n\times\Delta^1)\cup(K\times\{1\})$, with marking induced by $E$. Then $T_0=B$ and $\bigcup_nT_n=K\times\Delta^1$. For each attaching $\sigma$ use the map $\sigma\times\mathrm{id}$ from the minimally terminal-marked prism of Steps 2-4. It preserves markings because its designated edge maps to $\{\sigma(n)\}\times\Delta^1$, which is marked by the just-verified final-vertex hypothesis. Its boundary prism lies in $T_n$, and its terminal face lies in $K\times\{1\}$, so its restriction gives an attaching map from $D_n$.

source.place: Proposition 1.5.5.14, relative skeletal filtration; realizes the simplex-by-simplex reduction of HTT Lemma 3.2.1.9

proof.text: The resulting square, from the coproduct of the maps $(D_n,E_n\cap(D_n)_1)\hookrightarrow(\Delta^n\times\Delta^1,E_n)$ into $T_n\hookrightarrow T_{n+1}$, is a marked pushout. For the underlying square, take the boundary-cell pushout of Step 5 degreewise. Multiplying its sets by $(\Delta^1)_r$ preserves its quotient presentation: every relation is imposed separately at each fixed interval coordinate. Glue also the already present terminal face. Hence maps on $T_n$ and the new prisms which agree on $D_n$ give one and only one map in each degree; these maps commute with all simplicial operators because their restrictions do. This verifies the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], also when $\sigma$ identifies faces or vertices. For the marking, every nondegenerate marked target edge is vertical over a vertex in $A$. If that vertex lies in $Z_n$, its edge is already marked in $T_n$. For $n\geq1$ no new vertex is added by the boundary-cell pushout, since every vertex of $\Delta^n$ lies in its boundary. For $n=0$ every new vertex is a missing $0$-simplex and lies in $A$; its marked vertical edge is supplied by that cell's $e_0$. All degenerate target edges are marked, and images of cell and old markings are among $E$. Thus exactly the required target markings, and no others, are generated. Step 1 identifies the square as a marked pushout.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1.9, expansion of the marked gluing in the simplex-by-simplex reduction; degreewise argument supplied by Q74

proof.text: For each $n$, well-order the small set of its cells and attach the prisms of Step 6 one at a time, taking the degreewise marked union at limit ordinals. A map out of the resulting union is exactly a map on $T_n$ and one on each attached prism, agreeing on each $D_n$: successor stages impose that agreement, and limit stages impose compatibility of the restrictions. These are precisely the pushout data of Step 6, so uniqueness of the induced maps identifies the resulting map with $T_n\hookrightarrow T_{n+1}$. Each successor map is a pushout of the marked-anodyne map proved in Steps 2-4, so closure under pushouts and transfinite compositions in [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus] makes it marked anodyne. Concatenate these ordinal chains for $n=0,1,\ldots$; all indexing sets and their countable ordinal sum remain small in the fixed universes [def-weil-size-convention]. At the final union we obtain exactly $(B,E\cap B_1)\hookrightarrow(K\times\Delta^1,E)$ by Step 5 and the union rule of Step 1. If there are no cells this is the empty composite, an identity. Thus the required inclusion is marked anodyne.
